tooltip.title: Clinical Presentations of Psoriasis
tooltip.markdown: Psoriasis is a heterogeneous disease that can manifest in several distinct clinical forms. A patient can have more than one type at a time or over their lifetime. \[4, 16\]

tooltip.title: Plaque Psoriasis (Psoriasis Vulgaris)
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Prevalence:** Most common type, affecting 80-90% of patients. \[4, 16\]
-   **Manifestations:** Well-demarcated, raised, erythematous plaques with a silvery-white scale. \[22, 23\]
-   **Locations:** Typically affects extensor surfaces like elbows and knees, scalp, and the lumbosacral area. \[4\]

tooltip.title: Guttate Psoriasis
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Prevalence:** Affects about 8% of patients. \[16\]
-   **Manifestations:** Characterized by small, "drop-like," erythematous papules and plaques. \[16, 22\]
-   **Triggers:** Often appears suddenly after a streptococcal infection, especially in children and young adults. \[4\]

tooltip.title: Inverse (Flexural) Psoriasis
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Prevalence:** Affects about 25% of patients. \[16\]
-   **Manifestations:** Smooth, shiny, erythematous plaques without significant scaling. \[4\]
-   **Locations:** Occurs in skin folds such as the axillae, groin, inframammary, and gluteal cleft.

tooltip.title: Pustular Psoriasis
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Prevalence:** Affects about 3% of patients. \[16\]
-   **Manifestations:** Characterized by sterile, pus-filled pustules. Can be localized (e.g., palmoplantar pustulosis) or generalized (von Zumbusch), which is a medical emergency. \[4, 23\]

tooltip.title: Erythrodermic Psoriasis
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Manifestations:** A severe form involving generalized erythema and scaling of >90% of the body surface area. \[4\]
-   **Complications:** Can lead to severe systemic complications like dehydration, electrolyte imbalance, and cardiac failure, often requiring hospitalization.

tooltip.title: Nail Psoriasis
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Manifestations:** Can affect fingernails and toenails. Findings include pitting, onycholysis (lifting of the nail plate), subungual hyperkeratosis, and "oil drop" spots. \[23\]
-   **Association:** Strongly associated with the presence of psoriatic arthritis.
